method: Page retrieved twice. A firecrawl scrape was cleaned into /tmp/el.txt, and that cleaning step was found to have consumed a letter from words containing a doubled n (scanning -> sca ing, unplanned -> unpla ed). No quote was taken from it. The page was re-fetched directly with curl and converted to text (/tmp/el_clean.txt), which preserves those words; every claim below is verbatim-checked against that file. The HTML-to-text conversion also left a space before punctuation where a link tag closed mid-sentence ('the 4AT .'); that was normalised in the quoting file, which caught one claim and confirmed the remaining 102 unaffected.

claims.claim: Launched 1 May 2026 at the RACS Annual Scientific Congress
claims.source_text: The Standard was launched on 1 May 2026 at the Royal Australasian College of Surgeons (RACS) Annual Scientific Congress

claims.claim: Nine quality statements and a set of indicators
claims.source_text: nine quality statements describing safe and appropriate care … a set of indicators to support monitoring and quality improvement

claims.claim: Indicator 10b measures 30-day mortality
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy who died within 30 days of their surgery

claims.claim: Indicator 10c measures 90-day mortality
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy who died within 90 days of their surgery

claims.claim: Indicator 10a measures unplanned readmission within 30 days
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy, who had an unplanned readmission to any hospital within 30 days of discharge

claims.claim: The mortality risk referred to is estimated 30-day risk
claims.source_text: Estimated risk of death within 30 days of emergency laparotomy surgery

claims.claim: More than 15,000 Australians undergo emergency laparotomy each year
claims.source_text: Each year, more than 15,000 Australians undergo an emergency laparotomy (emergency abdominal surgery on the gastrointestinal tract) for time-critical conditions such as intra-abdominal infection, bowel obstruction, perforation, internal bleeding and ischaemia

claims.claim: Australian mortality estimates range from 6.2% to more than 20%
claims.source_text: Emergency laparotomy is a high-risk procedure with mortality estimates in Australia ranging from 6.2% to more than 20% in older adults and people with comorbidities

claims.claim: Estimated cost around $400 million per year
claims.source_text: The financial burden associated with the procedure is also significant at an estimated cost to Australian hospitals of around $400 million per year

claims.claim: More than half are aged over 65; more than 20% have sepsis on presentation
claims.source_text: More than half of patients who have an emergency laparotomy are aged over 65, and many of these older patients have a high level of frailty and multiple age-related comorbidities. More than 20% of emergency laparotomy patients have sepsis on presentation

claims.claim: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians twice as likely to be admitted for emergency surgery
claims.source_text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians are twice as likely to be admitted for emergency surgery as non-Indigenous Australians

claims.claim: 74% assigned urgency of 18 hours or less, 59% arrived in theatre in time
claims.source_text: Although 74% of patients undergoing emergency laparotomy were assigned a surgical urgency of 18 hours or less, just 59% of these patients arrived in theatre within the appropriate timeframe

claims.claim: Only 22% of older patients assessed post-operatively by geriatric medicine
claims.source_text: Only 22% of older patients were assessed post-operatively by a geriatric medicine specialist or team, despite evidence that such reviews are associated with lower mortality

claims.claim: Around 64% of highest-risk patients admitted to ICU or HDU post-operatively
claims.source_text: Around 64% of highest-risk patients were admitted to an intensive care or high dependency unit post-operatively, even though direct admission to critical care following surgery is known to support earlier recognition and management of post-operative complications

claims.claim: NELA credited with UK mortality reduction from 11.8% to 8.1% over ten years
claims.source_text: It was modelled on the United Kingdom's National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) which has been credited with substantial improvements in emergency laparotomy outcomes, including a reduction in mortality across the UK from 11.8% to 8.1% in its first ten years

claims.claim: Scope is adults 18 and over
claims.source_text: The Standard relates to the care that patients aged 18 and over should receive when they may need an emergency laparotomy

claims.claim: Scope includes patients for whom surgery is indicated who do not have surgery
claims.source_text: This includes patients for whom surgery is indicated but who do not go on to have surgery

claims.claim: Exclusions: trauma, appendicectomy, cholecystectomy, vascular, gynaecological, urological
claims.source_text: trauma laparotomy … emergency appendicectomy or cholecystectomy … vascular surgery including abdominal aortic aneurysm repair … primary gynaecological or urological emergency procedures

claims.claim: Lower-mortality procedures excluded on that basis
claims.source_text: more common procedures with significantly lower mortality, such as appendicectomy and cholecystectomy, are excluded

claims.claim: Bowel complications of earlier surgery in excluded specialties are included
claims.source_text: Emergency laparotomy for bowel complications of earlier surgery in these specialties is included

claims.claim: Mature minors note for 16 to 18 year olds
claims.source_text: While patients under 18 years of age are not in scope for this Standard, it is recognised that patients between 16 and 18 years are able to make decisions and give consent to medical treatment in certain circumstances

claims.claim: Statement 1 text
claims.source_text: A patient with symptoms suggestive of a time-critical intra-abdominal condition – including infection, perforation, bleeding, obstruction or ischaemia – is rapidly assessed and escalated in line with local protocols … In critically ill patients, investigations include blood lactate measurement

claims.claim: Statement 1 defers to the Sepsis Clinical Care Standard
claims.source_text: When sepsis is suspected, care is initiated urgently in accordance with the local sepsis pathway and the Sepsis Clinical Care Standard

claims.claim: Blood lactate is an independent predictor of mortality
claims.source_text: Blood lactate is an independent predictor of mortality for emergency laparotomy patients and is valuable in decision making about surgery

claims.claim: Do not delay surgical referral for pending investigations
claims.source_text: Do not delay surgical referral or review due to pending investigations or while awaiting investigation results

claims.claim: Patients at risk of delayed diagnosis are named
claims.source_text: Maintain a high index of suspicion … older patients, patients with a high degree of frailty or significant comorbidities, people with cognitive impairment, delirium or communication difficulties, and people who are immunocompromised

claims.claim: Statement 2 text including the one-hour verbal communication
claims.source_text: A patient with symptoms suggestive of a time-critical intra-abdominal condition has a computed tomography (CT) scan as soon as possible, with intravenous contrast unless contraindicated. The radiologist verbally communicates critical findings to the referring or responsible clinician, within one hour of the scan being performed. Acquiring a CT scan should not delay very urgent surgery

claims.claim: Do not delay contrast imaging for renal function results
claims.source_text: Be aware of current guidance for the use of contrast media in renal impairment: do not delay emergency imaging requiring IV contrast in order to obtain renal function testing results

claims.claim: CT must not delay very urgent surgery
claims.source_text: Ensure that accessing CT or awaiting results does not delay very urgent surgery

claims.claim: Verbal communication must be to a clinician who can act, and documented
claims.source_text: Communicate findings verbally to the referring and/or responsible clinician; this must be a clinician who can take appropriate clinical action. Document the discussion in the patient's medical imaging report, including who the results were discussed with

claims.claim: Consultant radiologist reporting preferred; senior trainee under supervision overnight
claims.source_text: Where emergency laparotomy may be indicated, review and reporting by a consultant radiologist before surgery is preferred. In some services, particularly overnight, this may be provided by a senior radiology trainee under appropriate supervision

claims.claim: Outsourced reporting must be covered by service agreements
claims.source_text: ensure that service agreements support local policies and procedures

claims.claim: Statement 3 text
claims.source_text: A patient being considered for an emergency laparotomy has their risk assessed and documented before surgery, using a validated, locally endorsed mortality risk prediction tool in addition to clinical judgement. In older patients, frailty, cognitive impairment and delirium are identified and documented pre-operatively using brief, validated tools

claims.claim: NELA calculator validated for use in Australia
claims.source_text: National Emergency Laparotomy Audit (NELA) risk calculator – which has been validated for use in Australia

claims.claim: ACS NSQIP and SORT also listed
claims.source_text: American College of Surgeons' National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS NSQIP) Surgical Risk Calculator … Surgical Outcome Risk Tool (SORT)

claims.claim: Frailty overrides the calculated mortality risk
claims.source_text: Frailty is independently associated with higher morbidity and mortality following emergency laparotomy and is not considered in some mortality risk calculators. Patients with frailty (for example, a Clinical Frailty Scale score of 5 or greater) should be considered high-risk regardless of their calculated mortality risk

claims.claim: 4AT for cognitive impairment and delirium risk
claims.source_text: Cognitive impairment and delirium risk (or presence): Use a brief, validated tool such as the 4AT. Perioperative delirium is associated with increased mortality, readmissions, perioperative complications and long-term cognitive decline

claims.claim: Risk models may over-estimate or under-estimate for the individual
claims.source_text: While risk scores can help guide discussions, they should be presented as an estimate and communication should be individualised, noting that mortality risk models may over-estimate or under-estimate risk for the individual

claims.claim: Assessment from 65, and from 45 for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients
claims.source_text: In patients aged 65 years and older – and on an individual basis for younger patients, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients aged 45 years and above, and patients with complex healthcare needs

claims.claim: Basis for the 45-year threshold is stated
claims.source_text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people may experience chronic health conditions that can impact their recovery earlier in life. Medical input to their care should also be considered on an individual basis from 45 years

claims.claim: The KICA is named for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients
claims.source_text: The Kimberley Indigenous Cognitive Assessment (KICA) has been developed specifically for Indigenous Australians and includes a remote and urban version

claims.claim: Statement 4 text
claims.source_text: When an emergency laparotomy is being considered, there is shared decision making about the patient's treatment plan … The patient's goals of care are discussed and documented before surgery, and updated throughout the perioperative period

claims.claim: Senior doctors involved when surgery may be non-beneficial
claims.source_text: When surgery may be non-beneficial, senior doctors are involved in discussing the likely outcomes, benefits and risks of surgical and non-surgical approaches to support shared decision making

claims.claim: BRAN and Best Case / Worst Case frameworks named
claims.source_text: the BRAN methodology ('Benefits, Risks, Alternatives, do Nothing') … Best Case / Worst Case scenarios framework

claims.claim: Risk scores cannot be used in isolation to make treatment decisions
claims.source_text: Risk assessment scores can help inform these discussions but must be interpreted with care and cannot be used in isolation to make treatment decisions

claims.claim: Structured shared decision making explores alternatives including palliative care
claims.source_text: there is structured shared decision making that considers whether to proceed with an emergency laparotomy, and explores alternative procedures or medical management options, which may include palliative and supportive care, ensuring the patient's and family's final treatment choices are informed by a realistic understanding of likely outcomes

claims.claim: Medical management pathway includes re-evaluation of surgery
claims.source_text: if the patient is proceeding with medical management, likely outcomes are explained, including whether surgical management will be re-evaluated

claims.claim: Statement 5 text
claims.source_text: A patient having an emergency laparotomy commences surgery within the timeframe specified by their assigned surgical urgency category

claims.claim: Urgency category assigned in accordance with the local framework
claims.source_text: assign a surgical urgency category in accordance with the local framework, to support the appropriate differentiation of urgency and prioritisation of theatre access

claims.claim: Source control within three hours in septic shock, six hours without
claims.source_text: Guidelines recommend that patients with septic shock receive surgical source control as soon as possible and within three hours. Patients with sepsis without septic shock should receive surgical source control within six hours

claims.claim: Mortality rises with every hour of delay in intra-abdominal sepsis
claims.source_text: For patients with an intra-abdominal source of sepsis, mortality rises with every hour of delay

claims.claim: Date and time of the decision to operate must be documented
claims.source_text: document the date and time of the decision to operate in the patient's healthcare record to enable accurate calculation of timely theatre access

claims.claim: Critically ill emergency patients prioritised over non-critical and elective surgery
claims.source_text: Systems should support the prioritisation of critically ill patients for emergency surgery before patients receiving non-critical or elective surgery

claims.claim: Statement 6 text with the 5% threshold
claims.source_text: A high-risk emergency laparotomy patient (mortality risk ≥5%) has a consultant surgeon and a consultant anaesthetist present in theatre during their surgery

claims.claim: Applies overnight
claims.source_text: This includes when urgent surgery must occur overnight

claims.claim: Supervising consultant physically present and free of other commitments
claims.source_text: If it is considered appropriate in a particular case for a non-consultant to perform the surgery or provide anaesthesia under supervision, the supervising consultant should be physically present in theatre and free of other commitments

claims.claim: Consultant absence associated with increased morbidity, mortality and length of stay
claims.source_text: The absence of consultants from operating theatres in emergency general surgery is associated with increased patient morbidity and mortality, and increased length of stay

claims.claim: Box 3 exists because the terms vary across Australia
claims.source_text: There is some variability across Australia in the use of the terms 'consultant surgeon' and 'consultant anaesthetist'

claims.claim: Consultant surgeon definition
claims.source_text: A surgeon who has been granted specialist registration by Ahpra and the Medical Board of Australia; and has been appointed to a consultant position or equivalent senior position by a healthcare service, reflective of their experience and seniority; and is operating within their locally defined scope of practice

claims.claim: Rural generalist anaesthetist equivalence
claims.source_text: In some rural settings, this may be a rural generalist anaesthetist who has been appointed to a consultant, or equivalent senior position, by their healthcare service

claims.claim: Statement 7 text with the 10% threshold
claims.source_text: A patient's post-operative critical care needs are considered based on mortality risk, frailty, comorbidities and clinical judgement. A patient with a mortality risk ≥10% is discussed with a consultant intensivist for consideration of direct post-operative admission to critical care

claims.claim: Case-by-case consideration between 5 and 10%
claims.source_text: Post-operative admission to critical care should be considered for all patients with a mortality risk ≥10% – and as needed on a case-by-case basis for patients with a risk between 5 and 10%

claims.claim: Critical care not to be denied on age or frailty alone
claims.source_text: Once a decision has been made to operate, a patient should not be denied critical care on the basis of age or frailty alone

claims.claim: Reason must be documented if a patient at risk 10% or more is not admitted
claims.source_text: If the patient has a mortality risk ≥10% and the decision is made not to admit to ICU or HDU post-operatively, document the reason in their record

claims.claim: Proactive ICU admission improves outcomes; unplanned ward admission has very high mortality
claims.source_text: Proactive admission of high-risk emergency general surgery patients to intensive care is associated with improved outcomes, including reduced mortality. Unplanned admission of patients to ICU from the ward following emergency gastrointestinal surgery is associated with very high mortality

claims.claim: Monitoring referred to the NSQHS acute deterioration standard
claims.source_text: National Safety and Quality Health Service (NSQHS) Standard for Recognising and Responding to Acute Deterioration

claims.claim: Enhanced care environment offered but undefined
claims.source_text: Where available, an enhanced care environment may be an appropriate location for continuous post-operative monitoring of some high-risk patients

claims.claim: Statement 8 text with the 72-hour clock from presentation
claims.source_text: An older patient who has an emergency laparotomy is proactively assessed and collaboratively managed by an appropriate physician, such as a geriatrician, skilled in the perioperative care of older adults. This assessment occurs as early as practicable and no later than 72 hours following presentation to hospital

claims.claim: CGA defined and associated with reduced mortality and length of stay
claims.source_text: Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA) is a multi-dimensional, interdisciplinary process used to assess an older person's medical, psychosocial and functional capabilities and develop a comprehensive management plan … CGA is associated with improved outcomes for older emergency general surgery patients, including reduced mortality and length of stay

claims.claim: Appropriate physician defined, including rural generalist
claims.source_text: In most settings, the 'appropriate physician' will be a geriatrician or general physician and will have expertise in the perioperative care of older adults. In regional, rural and remote settings, it may be a suitably skilled general practitioner or rural generalist

claims.claim: Also required after ward deterioration or step-down from critical care
claims.source_text: Timely assessment by an appropriate physician is also required for a patient undergoing emergency laparotomy following deterioration on the ward, or on step-down from critical care

claims.claim: Statement 9 text
claims.source_text: Before a person leaves hospital following an emergency laparotomy, an individualised care plan is developed describing their ongoing care needs. The plan addresses medicines, pain management, nutrition, wound care, and other services and supports needed to optimise recovery and reduce the risk of complications

claims.claim: Plan provided to patient and communicated to general practice at discharge
claims.source_text: The written plan is provided to the patient and their support people before they leave hospital. At the time of discharge, the plan is communicated to the patient's general practice, and to clinicians and other care providers involved in their ongoing care

claims.claim: My Health Record upload by default
claims.source_text: Enable uploading of the plan by default to My Health Record, which allows other clinicians to access details about the patient's care

claims.claim: Box 4 includes medicines and pain management
claims.source_text: Information about medicines (including new or changed medicines) and ongoing pain management strategies

claims.claim: Box 4 includes persistent delirium and VTE prevention
claims.source_text: Guidance on managing comorbidities during recovery, and on managing persistent delirium if present; strategies to prevent complications such as those related to infection or venous thromboembolism

claims.claim: Box 4 includes mental health advice
claims.source_text: Advice on responding to mental health concerns such as anxiety and loss of confidence

claims.claim: Box 4 sends sepsis survivors back to the sepsis standard
claims.source_text: For patients who have had sepsis, information on post-sepsis syndrome and available supports

claims.claim: Box 2 names transfer as a major source of risk
claims.source_text: For patients with acute abdominal symptoms who may require emergency laparotomy, transfers are a major source of risk, often delaying time-critical care and surgery

claims.claim: Operating on site with transfer afterwards may be necessary
claims.source_text: In some cases, transfer may not be possible or appropriate or may need to be deferred. The urgency of treatment or source control may necessitate that the emergency laparotomy be performed on-site, with transfer afterwards for further intervention and critical care

claims.claim: Transfer escalation is a consultant-to-consultant peer discussion
claims.source_text: This should be a consultant-to-consultant peer discussion, and involve multidisciplinary input as needed. If there is no consultant at the originating service, involve the most senior clinician responsible for the patient

claims.claim: Transfer discussion must name dying away from home
claims.source_text: Discussions should include, as appropriate, the risk of experiencing serious complications, the possibility of losing independence or dying away from home, and the likelihood of admission to intensive care

claims.claim: Box 1 does not discourage rural emergency laparotomy
claims.source_text: Its intent is not to prevent or discourage the provision of emergency laparotomy in rural and regional settings where a service is equipped and supported to do so, and where this is clinically appropriate

claims.claim: No benchmarks are set by the Commission
claims.source_text: No benchmarks are set for these indicators by the Commission

claims.claim: Indicator definitions are on METEOR
claims.source_text: The definitions required to collect and calculate indicator data are specified online at the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare's Metadata Online Registry

claims.claim: Indicator 1a
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy whose blood lactate was available at first surgical review

claims.claim: Indicator 2a
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy whose computed tomography scan results were verbally communicated by a radiologist to the referring or responsible clinician, within one hour of the scan being performed

claims.claim: Indicator 3a
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy whose risk was assessed using a validated mortality risk prediction tool and documented before surgery

claims.claim: Indicator 3b
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients aged 65 years or older who had an emergency laparotomy, whose frailty was assessed using a validated tool and documented before surgery

claims.claim: Indicator 4a
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients aged 65 years or older who had an emergency laparotomy, whose goals of care discussion was documented using a locally endorsed form before surgery

claims.claim: Indicator 5a
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy within the timeframe specified by their assigned surgical urgency category

claims.claim: Indicator 6a
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients with a preoperative mortality risk ≥5% who had an emergency laparotomy, where a consultant surgeon was present in theatre during surgery

claims.claim: Indicator 6b
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients with a preoperative mortality risk ≥5% who had an emergency laparotomy, where a consultant anaesthetist was present in theatre during surgery

claims.claim: Indicator 7a
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients with a preoperative mortality risk ≥10% who had an emergency laparotomy, with documentation that postoperative critical care was discussed with a consultant intensivist before surgery

claims.claim: Indicator 7b
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy, who had an unplanned admission to critical care from the ward

claims.claim: Indicator 8b
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients aged 65 years or older who had an emergency laparotomy, who were assessed within 72 hours of hospital presentation by an appropriate physician

claims.claim: Indicator 9b
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy, whose discharge summary was sent to their nominated primary care provider at the time of discharge from the hospital

claims.claim: Indicator 1a is published in a second wording on the statement page
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy whose blood lactate levels were available at first surgical review

claims.claim: Indicator 6a is published with the hyphenated spelling on the statement page
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients with a pre-operative mortality risk ≥5% who had an emergency laparotomy, where a consultant surgeon was present in theatre during surgery

claims.claim: Indicator 9a is published as separation in the list and discharge on the statement page
claims.source_text: Evidence of local arrangements for the development of a written individualised care plan for emergency laparotomy patients before separation from hospital … Evidence of local arrangements for the development of a written individualised care plan for emergency laparotomy patients before discharge from hospital

claims.claim: Indicator 9b is published in a second wording on the statement page
claims.source_text: Proportion of patients who had an emergency laparotomy, whose discharge summary was sent to their nominated primary healthcare provider at the time of discharge from hospital

claims.claim: ANZELA-QI is a clinical quality registry
claims.source_text: ANZELA-QI is a clinical quality registry providing feedback to participating hospitals on key evidence-based indicators of emergency laparotomy care

claims.claim: Participation in ANZELA-QI is encouraged, not required
claims.source_text: The Clinical Care Standard and ANZELA-QI indicators align where possible. Healthcare services that perform emergency laparotomies are encouraged to participate in the registry
